transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-09-29 15:00 PDT (Recorded)
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Dr. Leena Patel (CTO), Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng), Eva Stone (PM), Rajesh Iyer (Security)

Summary:
Brief: Scoping a POC to integrate Redwood's OpenAI-compatible API/SDK into Scythe Medical's clinical documentation assistant. Focus areas: success criteria (latency, accuracy, PHI handling), workload sizing (tokens/concurrency), benchmarks (p50/p95, cost), integration points (SDK, function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs), and timeline for a 4-6 week pilot.

Topics Covered:
- Target workloads and token distributions
- OpenAI-compatible endpoint usage and SDK mapping
- Function/tool calling behavior for EHR lookups and structured outputs (JSON schema validation)
- Dedicated vs hosted for PHI/HIPAA concerns; VPC/private deployment patterns
- Benchmark plan (1M token baseline run, p95 latency targets, quality evals)
- Next steps and action items

Transcript body (timestamps approximated, transcription not perfect):
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Today we want to lock down the POC scope — success criteria stuff, what workloads you have, and how we can plug in with our OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK. Leena, could you kick us off with the high level?

[00:18] Dr. Leena Patel (Scythe CTO): Sure, thanks Maya. Real quick context: we're building a clinical note assistant that helps clinicians draft notes from audio + patient context. The main concerns are PHI containment, 200 ms-ish token latency for interactive editing, and output structure — we need strict JSON for downstream ingestion. We're evaluating Redwood because we want consistent production latencies and an on-prem/VPC option if needed.

[00:40] Marco Ruiz (Lead ML Eng): To add, current traffic for the pilot team is about 120 concurrent clinicians at peak, average prompt length ~140 tokens, replies ~200 tokens. But when history is included we go up to 1k tokens occasionally. We can share traces.

[01:05] Samir Rao (Redwood SE): Great, that's helpful. For the POC we typically size three benchmark scenarios: 1) interactive edit flow (low latency, small tokens), 2) conversational thread with context (mid tokens), 3) bulk note generation (throughput-focused). Do those map to your workloads?

[01:25] Eva Stone (Product): Yes that maps well. The edit flow is the big one for UX; if it's slow clinicians complain.

[01:36] Rajesh Iyer (Security): From security, HIPAA compliance is mandatory. We need to know what goes to hosted logs, whether audit logs can be exported, and KMS options for key material. Also SSO/SAML + RBAC must be supported.

[01:54] Maya Chen: Understood. Redwood has Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) which keeps data in your network and offers KMS/HSM integrations; we can also provide SOC2 artifacts and audit log exports. We'll attach the security pack after this call.

[02:08] Jon Park (Redwood SE): On the API side, our OpenAI-compatible endpoints mimic the standard request/response shapes — you can hit /v1/completions or /v1/chat/completions with the same body. We also support function/tool calling; we can route a function result back into the model loop or return structured JSON via a schema. One note: the function schema enforcement is configurable — you can choose strict validation so any non-compliant model output is flagged or retried.

[02:39] Marco: That sounds good. For the structured output, we need a strict JSON schema for sections like problem list, assessment, plan. We also want the model to return a confidence score and provenance pointers to which EHR snippets were used. Can your function-calling return those fields?

[02:58] Samir: Yes — we recommend designing the schema up front. Our function-calling wrapper can accept a JSON schema and validate the model output. If the model deviates, we can auto-invoke a retry with a higher temperature penalty or fall back to a deterministic completions endpoint. We can also include token-level provenance metadata if you supply the EHR snippets as context with unique IDs.

[03:20] Dr. Leena: On latency, we talked about 200 ms per token target earlier. Is that realistic on shared hosted endpoints?

[03:30] Jon: For small tokens/interactive flows, hosted can hit low-latency ranges but it depends on burst patterns. For guaranteed p95 under 250 ms we usually suggest a Dedicated capacity pilot so you have reserved GPU pools. If you want private VPC and HIPAA, most customers choose Private deployment or Dedicated in a covered region.

[03:52] Maya: Important tradeoff: Dedicated gives predictability (and SLOs) but costs more; hosted is faster to start. For the POC we can start hosted with strict routing to a high-performance instance type, and then run a Dedicated pilot in parallel if you need a hard SLA.

[04:10] Marco: Cost-wise, what does a dedicated pilot look like for our scale (120 concurrent, average 340 tokens per request incl history)?

[04:20] Maya: We'll provide an estimate but rough math: with batching and prefix cache you often see effective token costs drop 20-40% compared to naive serving. For a 2-month pilot we'll lay out both per-token hosted estimate and reserved capacity pricing.

[04:35] Rajesh: Also need to confirm data retention and can we turn off logging for PHI?

[04:44] Samir: Yes — in Private deployments and certain Dedicated configs we can disable persistence of request bodies in the control plane; audit logs still exist per your retention policy and can be exported to your S3 or SIEM. We'll detail the options in the security pack.

[05:00] Eva: For the integration flow: we prefer to call an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint from our backend, get structured JSON back, then pass it to our internal validators. What's the recommended SDK path?

[05:12] Jon: Use Redwood's OpenAI-compatible SDK wrapper — almost drop-in for your existing OpenAI calls. We have examples for function-calling and JSON schema enforcement. We'll share a sample repo with both sync REST calls and streaming responses (useful for the UI to render tokens). Streaming support is available on both hosted and Dedicated.

[05:36] Marco: If we stream tokens to the clinician UI, do you provide partial JSON validation or only at the end?

[05:45] Samir: Typically you receive token stream for UX, but schema validation happens at completion. For stricter flows, we support chunked function calls: the model can emit structured chunks conforming to a streaming schema, and the SDK will buffer and validate as it completes. There can be a small tradeoff to latency.

[06:05] Dr. Leena: Benchmarking — can we run a 1M-token baseline to evaluate latency and cost? What do you need from us?

[06:15] Jon: We'll need canonical prompt sets, typical history lengths, and a sample client that simulates your concurrency. Ideally token histograms and a 24-48 hour trace. We'll supply a JMeter-style benchmark script that hits the OpenAI-compatible endpoints and records p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and error rates. We'll run it on hosted and on a Dedicated pilot config.

[06:42] Marco: We'll prepare those traces. For quality measurement, we want automated evals: pass/fail against a set of golden notes with tolerances. Can Redwood hook into our eval harness?

[06:55] Samir: Yes — we can ingest your eval set. We also have a basic quality monitoring dashboard that ties to prompt sets; we'll instrument automatic regression alerts when quality drops past thresholds.

[07:10] Eva: Timeline question: how long to get a POC running end-to-end?

[07:16] Maya: Typical timeline: 1 week to onboard and share artifacts, 1 week to get SDK integrated and run a smoke test, 2 weeks of benchmarks + quality tuning, and 1 week for consolidation and a decision meeting. So roughly 5 weeks. If you require Private on-prem setup, add 1-2 weeks for infra coordination.

[07:40] Rajesh: For HIPAA we need BAAs and potentially a private control plane — what's Redwood's stance?

[07:48] Maya: We sign BAAs for Private and some Dedicated customers; we'll share legal templates. The Private deployment keeps the control plane in your VPC and you manage keys, which is usually required for PHI-sensitive workloads.

[07:58] Dr. Leena: Ok. For success criteria we want: p95 latency <= 350 ms for interactive edits, accuracy measured as >= 85% pass rate on structured sections, no PHI leakage, and total cost under threshold X (we'll provide baseline). Are those feasible?

[08:18] Samir: Those look concrete. p95 350 ms is achievable with Dedicated or well-provisioned hosted instances and aggressive caching. The accuracy target depends on prompt engineering and model variant; we'll run a quick set of evals to show baseline.

[08:33] Marco: About model variants — do you recommend specific open models? We currently have in-house fine-tuned checkpoints but want Redwood for serving.

[08:41] Jon: We support a selection of open models and custom model imports. For tight latency + structured output, we often recommend a high-throughput quantized variant or a smaller tuned model if it meets quality. We can run A/Bs during the POC to compare latency/cost/quality tradeoffs.

[09:00] Eva: Any limitations on tool calling — e.g., calling our internal patient lookup service as a function?

[09:08] Samir: No, you can define a function schema for the patient lookup. But note: if the function needs to access PHI, that call should happen inside your network (we can proxy) or on a Private deployment so the data doesn't leave your VPC.

[09:25] Dr. Leena: Good. For logging and audit we want immutable logs and ability to run forensic search. Can we get log retention and export options?

[09:33] Maya: Yes — audit logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM, and retention policies are configurable in Dedicated/Private. We'll document the options in the security pack.

[09:46] Marco: About the SDK: does it preserve OpenAI request IDs or generate Redwood-specific IDs? We need traceability to our requests.

[09:55] Jon: The SDK echoes back your request_id if you pass one; we also attach a Redwood trace id. Both are surfaced in the response headers for cross-correlation.

[10:05] Eva: Are there any gotchas you recommend we watch for during integration?

[10:10] Samir: A few common ones: 1) token accounting — remember that context + history counts; 2) temperature/retry loops can blow token budgets if not bounded; 3) streaming + strict schema can be tricky, so start with end-of-response validation then move to streaming validation once stable.

[10:28] Maya: Also watch for KV cache benefits — if you prefix identical static context, caching can reduce cost significantly. We'll show configuration suggestions in Redwood Optimize runbook.

[10:40] (brief cross-talk/noise)

[10:48] Dr. Leena: Quick question — for PHI masking, do you provide a redaction layer or should we do it client-side?

[10:54] Samir: We recommend client-side redaction as primary; Redwood has optional pre-processing hooks and token-level masking utilities you can run in your pipeline. For Private deployments you can also integrate a per-tenant redaction service.

[11:08] Marco: For the POC benchmarks, can you run both streaming and non-streaming tests?

[11:12] Jon: Yes — we'll run both, measure p50/p95 token emission latency for streaming, and end-to-end completion latency for non-streaming. We'll include token costs and effective throughput metrics.

[11:24] Maya: Ok let's summarize next steps — quick recap so nothing gets lost.

[11:28] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Action recap: Redwood will send security pack and BAA template; Samir/Jon will post SDK example repo with OpenAI-compatible call shapes and function-calling examples; Jon will prepare a benchmark script and baseline config; Scythe will provide prompt sets and traces by 2025-10-03; we'll aim to run benchmarks week of 2025-10-06 and have a decision meeting ~2025-10-13.

[11:51] Dr. Leena: That timeline works for us. One ask — include a sample structured JSON schema in the repo so our validators can test early.

[11:59] Maya: Will do.

[12:03] Eva: And please include sample cURL and streaming client snippets for our frontend engineers.

[12:07] Jon: Yep, we'll include streaming examples with reconnect semantics and backpressure notes.

[12:14] Rajesh: Also include SSO/SAML setup docs and key rollover procedures.

[12:18] Priya Nair (Redwood CSM): We'll coordinate the architecture review invite for security and infra — target 2025-10-07.

[12:25] Dr. Leena: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the artifacts.

[12:30] (meeting ends)
